scope: Analytical mapping of potential financial-stability and institutional risk channels arising from autonomous or agentic AI use in financial services. This is not a register of confirmed agent-caused losses.
methodology: Risk channels are grounded in official financial-stability publications on AI and financial-sector vulnerabilities. Agent-specific pathways are MONAISEC analytical extensions unless a source explicitly discusses agentic systems. No probability, severity or aggregate risk score is assigned. Impact depends on deployment context, autonomy, permissions, transaction scale, market conditions, substitutability, concentration and controls.

records.title: Market integrity and correlated behaviour
records.summary: Multiple agents using similar models, signals, data or optimisation objectives may converge on comparable actions. Under stressed conditions, automated responses could reinforce price moves, reduce diversity of liquidity provision or accelerate disorderly market dynamics.
records.agent_pathway: Autonomous trading or portfolio agents independently react to the same news, risk thresholds or model outputs, creating correlated orders or feedback loops.
records.transmission: Common signals or model behaviour → correlated orders → price impact and volatility → liquidity deterioration or market disruption.
monitoring_indicators: Similarity of model/provider use across firms
control_themes: Human escalation for exceptional market conditions
records.evidence_class: Officially identified AI vulnerability; agent-specific pathway is analytical
records.evidence_note: The FSB identifies market correlations as a potential AI-related vulnerability. The autonomous multi-agent pathway described here is a MONAISEC scenario, not a claim of a documented agent-caused market event.

sources.title: FSB — The Financial Stability Implications of Artificial Intelligence (14 Nov 2024)
IMF — Global Financial Stability Report, October 2024, Chapter 3

records.title: Liquidity stress and automated deleveraging
records.summary: Agents that manage collateral, treasury, margin or portfolios may respond rapidly to liquidity thresholds. If many systems de-risk simultaneously, local funding pressure can become broader asset sales, collateral calls or reduced market liquidity.
records.agent_pathway: Treasury, collateral or portfolio agents trigger withdrawals, asset sales, margin actions or credit-line changes in response to shared signals or incomplete state information.
records.transmission: Trigger or forecast shock → simultaneous automated de-risking → asset sales and funding demand → price pressure and liquidity stress.
records.evidence_class: Financial-stability transmission channel supported; agent-specific pathway is analytical
records.evidence_note: Official financial-stability analysis documents how leverage, liquidity mismatches and correlated actions can amplify shocks. The use of autonomous agents as the trigger is a scenario for testing.

sources.title: IMF — Global Financial Stability Report, October 2024
Bank of England — Financial Stability Report, June 2024

records.title: Operational disruption of critical financial services
records.summary: An agent failure, unsafe tool call, compromised dependency or runaway workflow may disrupt payments, trading, customer servicing, reconciliation or other critical operations. The impact depends on service criticality, containment and recovery capability.
records.agent_pathway: An agent with write access invokes a faulty or malicious workflow across payment, ledger, trading or case-management systems, or exhausts shared service capacity.
records.transmission: Agent or dependency failure → process interruption or corrupted state → service outage and backlogs → client, counterparty or infrastructure disruption.
records.evidence_class: Established operational-resilience concern; agent-specific pathway is analytical
records.evidence_note: DORA establishes requirements for ICT risk management, incident handling, testing and third-party risk in the EU financial sector. This record analyses how agentic systems could enter those operational risk pathways; it does not assert a confirmed agent-caused outage.

sources.title: European Commission — Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA)
IMF — Artificial Intelligence and Cybersecurity in the Financial Sector (30 Jun 2026)

records.title: Fraud, unauthorised transactions and financial crime
records.summary: Agents may be manipulated into initiating payments, changing beneficiary details, approving refunds, generating fraudulent instructions or facilitating synthetic identity and social-engineering schemes. The risk increases when identity, intent and transaction authority are not independently verified.
records.agent_pathway: Prompt injection, compromised credentials or deceptive content persuades an agent to execute a payment or alter a customer or counterparty record.
records.transmission: Manipulated instruction or identity → agent action → unauthorised transfer or control bypass → direct loss and downstream disputes.
control_themes: Immutable audit trails and fraud monitoring
records.evidence_class: AI-enabled fraud risk identified by official sources; agent scenario is analytical
records.evidence_note: The FSB identifies AI-enabled fraud and disinformation as financial-sector vulnerabilities. The specific autonomous payment scenario is a MONAISEC analytical test case.

sources.title: FSB — The Financial Stability Implications of Artificial Intelligence (14 Nov 2024)
MAS — Guidelines on AI Risk Management for Financial Institutions (7 Oct 2026)

records.title: Credit, underwriting and exposure misallocation
records.summary: Agents supporting origination, underwriting, limit management or collections may propagate inaccurate, manipulated or biased information into credit decisions. If widely deployed models share data or assumptions, errors may become correlated across portfolios or institutions.
records.agent_pathway: An agent gathers evidence, updates borrower records, recommends limits or triggers decisions using poisoned, stale or incomplete data and insufficient human review.
records.transmission: Data or reasoning error → incorrect risk assessment or action → mispriced credit and concentrated exposures → losses or unfair outcomes.
records.evidence_class: AI model and data risk supported by official analysis; agent workflow is analytical
records.evidence_note: FSB and IMF publications identify model risk, data quality and governance as relevant financial-sector vulnerabilities. The agent-mediated workflow is a proposed risk pathway, not a documented loss event.

sources.title: FSB — The Financial Stability Implications of Artificial Intelligence (14 Nov 2024)

records.title: Third-party concentration and common-provider dependency
records.summary: Financial institutions may depend on a small set of model, cloud, compute, data, orchestration or agent-platform providers. A shared provider outage, compromise, policy change or capacity constraint can affect multiple institutions at once.
records.agent_pathway: Several firms deploy agents built on the same model APIs, orchestration platforms, MCP/tool providers or cloud infrastructure, creating correlated operational dependencies.
records.transmission: Common provider disruption or compromise → simultaneous loss or degradation of agent capability → multi-firm operational stress → potential systemic spillovers.
records.evidence_note: The FSB explicitly identifies third-party dependencies and service-provider concentration as potential systemic vulnerabilities, and its 2025 monitoring report discusses indicators and data gaps. Agent-platform concentration is a MONAISEC extension of this issue.

sources.title: FSB — Monitoring Adoption of AI and Related Vulnerabilities in the Financial Sector (10 Oct 2025)

records.title: Cyber compromise and cross-institution propagation
records.summary: Agent-enabled cyber activity may accelerate vulnerability discovery, exploitation, credential abuse or lateral movement. Shared infrastructure and interconnected financial services can turn a local compromise into a broader disruption if containment is weak.
records.agent_pathway: A compromised agent, tool connector or service identity is used to access sensitive systems, exfiltrate data or execute actions across connected environments.
records.transmission: Compromise → privileged access or data exfiltration → lateral movement or service disruption → counterparties and shared infrastructure affected.
records.evidence_class: Officially identified AI-amplified cyber and systemic channel; agent scenario is analytical
records.evidence_note: IMF 2026 analysis warns that AI can increase the speed and scale of cyber risk and emphasises limiting blast radius. This entry applies those findings to agent identities and tool chains as a research scenario.

sources.title: IMF — Artificial Intelligence and Cybersecurity in the Financial Sector (30 Jun 2026)
IMF — Financial Stability Risks Mount as Artificial Intelligence Fuels Cyberattacks (7 May 2026)

records.title: Conduct, consumer protection and accountability failure
records.summary: Customer-facing or decision-support agents may provide misleading information, make unauthorised commitments, apply unsuitable recommendations or obscure responsibility for decisions. Failures can scale rapidly across customers and channels.
records.agent_pathway: An agent communicates with customers, changes account settings or makes product recommendations without adequate disclosure, suitability checks, escalation or accountable ownership.
records.transmission: Inaccurate or unauthorised agent interaction → customer reliance or harmful decision → complaints, remediation and conduct exposure.
records.evidence_class: General AI governance and conduct concern; agent pathway is analytical
records.evidence_note: Regulatory and supervisory frameworks continue to apply to financial firms using AI. This entry is a MONAISEC analysis of how agent autonomy may complicate existing accountability and consumer-outcome obligations.

sources.title: FCA — AI in financial services: good practice and areas for improvement (19 Oct 2026)
FSB — Sound Practices for the Responsible Adoption of AI in the Financial Sector (15 Oct 2026)

records.title: Data confidentiality, integrity and decision contamination
records.summary: Agents can access, transform, retain and transmit sensitive information across multiple tools. Prompt injection, memory poisoning or unsafe retrieval may cause disclosure, corruption of records or decisions based on manipulated information.
records.agent_pathway: An agent retrieves confidential customer or market data, stores it in persistent memory, or sends it to an unauthorised endpoint after following malicious instructions embedded in content.
records.transmission: Compromised context or data path → unauthorised disclosure or corrupted record → privacy, integrity and decision failures → legal and financial consequences.
records.evidence_class: Established AI data/model governance concerns; agent pathway is analytical
records.evidence_note: FSB identifies model risk, data quality and governance as AI-related vulnerabilities. The agent memory and tool-mediated exfiltration pathways are analytical applications of recognised agentic threat patterns.

records.title: Systemic contagion and confidence effects
records.summary: A severe agent-related event could propagate through interconnected institutions, shared service providers, common trading strategies or confidence-sensitive channels. The systemic outcome is conditional and should be tested rather than presumed.
records.agent_pathway: A common model or provider failure, cyber compromise or correlated autonomous response affects multiple institutions or critical infrastructure during an already stressed market environment.
records.transmission: Common shock → correlated institutional response or service interruption → counterparty and market spillovers → confidence and financial-stability effects.
records.evidence_class: Systemic transmission channels supported; agent-triggered event is hypothetical
records.evidence_note: The FSB and IMF identify channels through which AI-related vulnerabilities and cyber incidents could affect financial stability. This record is a conditional scenario, not a claim that an agentic event has caused systemic contagion.
